Sequential spawn preflight is not a concurrent regression. A future correct whole-run serialization could prevent B publishing until A is released; do not mislabel this as a deadlock or race failure.
no_network_contract: Use disposable exact-SHA checkout and temp shared archive; T=1700000000000; rowB PIT-visible as in existing sequential spawn fixture.

Instrument only runner.atomic_write_json for anata_latest.json; child A loads empty archive and positively signals A_PAUSED immediately before its stale handoff write. Bound waits/joins; no sleeps as causal proof.

Start separate APPENDER and B process; positively witness rowB durable in observations.jsonl and B reaching a publication phase. If B publishes rowB before A release, parent must positively parse persisted rowB before releasing A; then assert rowB remains after A completes. Missing B-published-before-A witness is INCONCLUSIVE, not PASS.

If B is demonstrably serialized behind an explicit lock phase, release A then require B to complete and persist rowB; label SERIALIZED_PASS only with positive lock/phase witness, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.

If A overwrites witnessed newer rowB, label RED even if sequential recovery C later restores it. Execute C to classify recoverability; record process exitcodes, phases, before/after handoff and archive hashes. Do not require three-file atomic snapshot without consumer contract.
